artworks.title: Mnemosyne (The Lamp of Memory)
artworks.description: An oil by Dante Gabriel Rossetti in the Delaware Art Museum, also called The Lamp of Memory. The Titaness of recollection holds a lamp and wears a dark, heavy gaze — Pre-Raphaelite Memory as longing made flesh, the mother of the Muses reimagined as a late-Victorian icon of remembrance.

artworks.title: Jupiter and Mnemosyne
artworks.description: An oil by Jacob de Wit in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (SK-A-3886). Jupiter, disguised as a shepherd, courts Mnemosyne in a pastoral landscape while his eagle wheels above — the nine nights that will father the Muses staged as Rococo gallantry, Memory herself the object of divine pursuit.

artworks.title: Wall Mosaic of Mnemosyne
artworks.year: Third quarter of the 2nd century AD
artworks.description: A Roman wall mosaic of the mid–late second century AD naming Mnemosyne, Memory personified among the powers that govern recollection. Tesserae rather than canvas: the Titaness as a cult and decorative presence in the Imperial house, the goddess whose name still anchors every mnemonic.

popCulture.title: Mnemonic
popCulture.description: English mnemonic descends from Mnemosyne — Memory herself as the root of every memory-aid, from schoolroom acronyms to orators' palaces of memory.

popCulture.title: Mnemosyne
popCulture.creator: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
popCulture.description: Rossetti's Pre-Raphaelite Mnemosyne — also called The Lamp of Memory — made the Titaness a late-Victorian icon of recollection and longing.
